stories.title: Bitcoin dips below $80,000 as US cuts Middle East embassy staff
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell under $80,000 on Saturday to a nine-day low. Phemex News links the slide to reported US evacuations of personnel from Middle East embassies and military bases amid Iran threats. The fall forced many leveraged traders out of their bets.
points: Bitcoin fell to a nine-day low of about $79,750, per CryptoPotato.
About $670M of leveraged positions were liquidated (forcibly closed) over 24 hours, per CoinGlass data cited by CryptoPotato.
US embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE reduced staff, and non-essential staff were ordered out of Saudi Arabia, per AP.
Ether and Solana fell harder: CoinGecko showed ETH down 4.3% and SOL down 4.8% over 24 hours at about 16:00 UTC.
The Fed decides on Wed 28 Oct at 2:00pm ET with rates at 3.75-4.00%; 94 of 100 economists in a Reuters poll expect a hold.

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs lose money for a second straight day
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, funds that hold bitcoin for stock-market investors, saw another $137.9 million leave on Friday 23 Oct after a $635.6 million outflow on Thursday. Strong buying earlier in the week means the week as a whole still ended slightly positive.
points: Friday's net outflow was $137.9M, led by BlackRock's IBIT (-$110.3M) and Fidelity's FBTC (-$31.8M), per Farside Investors.
Thursday's $635.6M outflow was the largest daily outflow since June, per The Block. IBIT lost $254.1M, FBTC $217.5M and Ark's ARKB $109.4M that day, per Farside Investors.
Before Thursday the week had inflows of $526.7M on Monday, $23.2M on Tuesday and $524.8M on Wednesday, per Farside Investors.
Farside's five daily figures add up to about +$301M for the week.

sources.label: The Block: Bitcoin ETFs swing back to net outflows

stories.title: Circle shareholder sues Trump over UAE-linked crypto deals
stories.summary: A Circle shareholder has filed a lawsuit in federal court in Washington claiming that UAE-linked payments to Trump-family crypto ventures broke the Constitution's ban on officials taking foreign payments, and steered business away from Circle's USDC stablecoin. These are allegations; no court has ruled.
points: The suit was filed on 22 Oct by J. Benjamin Greenberg, a former Circle employee who holds 10,000 shares, per CryptoSlate.
It alleges a vehicle tied to Sheikh Tahnoon paid $500M for 49% of World Liberty Financial, per CryptoSlate.
It says MGX's $2B Binance investment was settled in World Liberty's USD1 stablecoin, costing Circle $70M-82M a year in potential revenue, per CryptoSlate.
Binance and World Liberty deny the claims, per CryptoSlate.

briefs.title: Initia's network is still halted after a $2.7M exploit
